text:
Maintaining U.S. Space Superiority: Addressing China’s Reusable Spaceplane Advances Through Conservative Principles of Deterrence and Technological Primacy

Dr. Joel P. Rutkowski
Thursday, October 29, 2026

Executive Summary

The October 26, 2026, release of the Defense Intelligence Agency’s “Challenges to Security in Space” report (https://t.co/NAELuhpeFY), which includes a Maxar Technologies image of China’s reusable experimental spacecraft (commonly associated with the Shenlong program), confirms that the People’s Republic of China (PRC) has fielded a functional uncrewed orbital spaceplane capable of multi-month missions, rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO), and object deployment/recapture. This capability, demonstrated across four missions since September 2020, parallels the U.S. Boeing X-37B Orbital Test Vehicle but does not yet match its cumulative flight heritage or experimental sophistication.

From a conservative national-security perspective rooted in realism, U.S. technological and military primacy, and deterrence by denial and punishment, the appropriate response is not alarmism or unilateral restraint but accelerated investment in resilient architectures, space domain awareness, counterspace options, commercial innovation, and alliances with free and open societies. Unverifiable arms-control proposals favored by Beijing should be rejected. The United States must treat space as a contested warfighting domain and preserve freedom of action for itself and its partners.

I. Introduction and Background

The Defense Intelligence Agency-DIA’s 2026 unclassified report (information cutoff July 2026) continues a series begun in 2019 that documents the growing spectrum of Chinese and Russian counterspace capabilities—kinetic, directed-energy, electronic, cyber, and on-orbit. The inclusion of a high-resolution Maxar image of the Chinese spaceplane (taken in 2024 during its third mission) provides the clearest public confirmation yet of the vehicle’s configuration, including rear-deployed solar arrays. Mission data align with independent tracking: a two-day 2020 flight, a 276-day 2022–2023 flight involving close approaches, a 268-day 2023–2024 flight with object interactions, and a fourth launch in February 2026 that has included repeated release and apparent recapture of a companion object. (https://t.co/Hdo28T8GAp)

China officially describes these flights as tests of reusable technologies for the peaceful use of space. Dual-use potential for inspection, servicing, or interference is evident and consistent with broader PLA modernization goals of denying U.S. space-enabled advantages in a conflict, particularly in the Indo-Pacific.

II.Literature Review: Evolution of Reusable Spaceplanes and Strategic Competition (1950–2026)

Reusable spaceplane concepts predate the Space Age. Eugen Sänger’s 1930s–1940s work on hypersonic boost-glide vehicles and the Silbervogel concept influenced post-war thinking. In the 1950s, Wernher von Braun and others proposed winged ferry rockets. The U.S. North American X-15 (1959–1968) achieved the first suborbital spaceflights by a reusable winged vehicle, generating foundational hypersonic and reentry data. The canceled X-20 Dyna-Soar program (late 1950s–early 1960s) aimed at a military spaceplane for reconnaissance, satellite inspection, and potential strike roles—precisely the dual-use missions now of concern.(https://t.co/VgoPnIK70Q)

The Space Shuttle (1981–2011) demonstrated partial reusability at scale but proved operationally expensive and vulnerable. The Soviet Buran flew once uncrewed in 1988 before cancellation. Post-Shuttle, the U.S. X-37 program (originating at NASA in 1999, transferred to Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency-DARPA and then the Air Force) produced the operational X-37B: first orbital flight 2010, cumulative >4,200 days across eight missions by 2026, longest single flight 908 days, and demonstrated capabilities including service modules, small-satellite deployment, aerobraking, laser communications, and quantum inertial sensors. Dimensions are approximately 29 ft long with a 15 foot wingspan.(https://t.co/xBbJSLEso7)

China’s program traces to the 863 Plan and Project 863-706 (Shenlong). Drop tests from an H-6 bomber appeared by 2007; a reported suborbital flight occurred around 2011. Orbital operations began in 2020 with progressive duration increases and RPO demonstrations, reflecting China’s civil-military fusion model and rapid iteration. Broader literature on reusability (e.g., reviews of European IXV, commercial Dream Chaser concepts, and booster recovery) underscores that partial reusability of the orbited vehicle, as practiced by both the X-37B and China’s spacecraft, offers cost and responsiveness advantages for experimental and potentially operational missions while full single-stage-to-orbit remains elusive.(https://t.co/pq4cJFLiFl)

DIA reports (2019, 2022, 2026) and Space Force assessments consistently identify China as the pacing long-term threat and Russia as the acute near-term threat in counterspace. Historical Cold War lessons—mutual vulnerability, the failure of unenforced treaties, and the value of technological offset—remain relevant. Commercial proliferation (SpaceX, others) has altered the cost curve, favoring states that integrate private innovation with national security priorities.

III. Current Assessment: Capabilities Comparison

China has closed much of the conceptual gap in uncrewed reusable orbital vehicles within six years of first flight. Demonstrated Recovery Point Objective-RPO, multi-month endurance, and runway recovery are operationally significant. However, the U.S. retains advantages in total flight time, experimental payload transparency (selective), higher-orbit operations (e.g., OTV-7), and integration with a larger commercial launch and satellite ecosystem. Both systems are dual-use; neither is a pure “space bomber,” and claims of immediate kinetic ground-attack roles are overstated given payload and energy constraints. The strategic concern is the platform’s contribution to China’s overall counterspace toolkit and its signaling of indigenous mastery of reentry, autonomy, and on-orbit maneuvering.

IV. Application of Conservative Principles

Conservative national-security principles prioritize:

- Realism and primacy: Adversaries act on interests, not abstract norms. Space is already a warfighting domain; the United States must retain the ability to operate freely while denying the same to peer competitors.
- Deterrence by denial and punishment: Resilience reduces the value of a first strike; credible counterspace options raise the cost of aggression. Ambiguity can aid deterrence but must be paired with demonstrated capability.
- Skepticism of unverifiable restraint: Chinese and Russian proposals for “no first placement” of weapons or broad bans have historically coincided with their own development of dual-use systems. Such agreements would constrain the United States more than adversaries who practice civil-military fusion and opacity.
- Commercial and alliance leverage: Free-market innovation (launch, satellites, sensors) and partnerships with democratic allies multiply U.S. strength without centralized industrial policy.
- Limited government focused on core missions: Defense of the commons and protection of U.S. and allied space-enabled warfighting and economic functions are legitimate national priorities.

V. Policy Recommendations

1. Accelerate U.S. reusable and experimental programs: Sustain X-37B flight rate and transition proven technologies into operational architectures. Fund next-generation vehicles with greater payload, endurance, and rapid-turnaround capacity. Integrate quantum navigation, laser communications, and advanced propulsion.
2. Prioritize resilience and space domain awareness: Expand proliferated LEO constellations, on-orbit servicing, and rapid reconstitution. Invest in multi-phenomenology tracking to characterize RPO and anomalous maneuvers in near real time.
3. Field and exercise counterspace options: Develop discriminate, reversible, and (where necessary) kinetic capabilities that avoid debris generation where possible. Public acknowledgment of on-orbit defensive weapons, as recently stated by senior officials, strengthens deterrence without full disclosure.
4. Leverage commercial sector: Streamline acquisition, expand dual-use partnerships, and protect intellectual property and supply chains from adversarial influence. Commercial imagery (as with Maxar) already contributes to transparency.
5. Strengthen alliances: Deepen AUKUS, Five Eyes, and Indo-Pacific partnerships on space situational awareness, resilient architectures, and norms among like-minded states. Reject frameworks that grant equal voice to revisionist powers without reciprocal transparency.
6. Reject disadvantageous arms control: Engage in confidence-building only where verification is feasible and mutual. Prioritize national and allied freedom of action over symbolic treaties.

Discussion

The emergence of China’s reusable experimental spaceplane program—authoritatively detailed in the Defense Intelligence Agency’s 2026 assessment and underscored by high-resolution Maxar orbital imagery—marks a watershed moment in the militarization and strategic contestation of Earth’s orbital commons. For decades, the United States maintained undisputed technological primacy in uncrewed reusable lifting-body operations, epitomized by the U.S. Space Force’s X-37B Orbital Test Vehicle. Today, that monopoly has formally ended. The People’s Republic of China has demonstrated a deliberate, methodical, and technologically sophisticated trajectory: progressing from a two-day maiden flight in September 2020 to multi-month, highly complex orbital missions featuring autonomous proximity operations, object release, and apparent recapture capabilities.

When viewed through the lens of realist national security and historical precedent, these developments are neither surprising nor anomalous. As established in the broader trajectory of hypersonic and spaceplane evolution—from Eugen Sänger’s early concepts and Wernher von Braun’s ferry designs to the canceled X-20 Dyna-Soar—winged, maneuverable spacecraft have always represented the holy grail of strategic flexibility. They combine the unpredictable trajectory of ballistic systems with the operational versatility of aircraft. Beijing’s strategy relies heavily on civil-military fusion, leveraging nominal civilian research programs to rapidly field dual-use assets designed explicitly to challenge U.S. command of the space domain.

However, an objective comparative assessment reveals a nuanced strategic picture. While Beijing has successfully closed the conceptual and functional gap in baseline orbital flight and rendezvous mechanics, the United States retains decisive structural advantages. The X-37B boasts an unmatched cumulative flight heritage exceeding 4,200 days, superior high-altitude operating capabilities, and a far more mature integration with both national security architectures and a booming commercial space ecosystem. Furthermore, neither the American nor the Chinese platform functions as a rudimentary "space bomber." The fundamental physical constraints of payload capacity, thermal dissipation, and orbital energy dynamics make direct kinetic ground-attack from these vehicles highly inefficient compared to traditional intercontinental ballistic missiles or fractional orbital bombardment systems.

The true strategic threat of China’s spaceplane lies elsewhere: as an active instrument of counterspace coercion, satellite inspection, electronic interference, and gray-zone dominance. In a contested Indo-Pacific theater, any adversary capability that threatens American space-enabled command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (C4ISR) architecture directly undermines conventional deterrence. If U.S. decision-makers cannot trust the resilience of their orbital constellations, the entire framework of power projection in the Western Pacific frays.

Final Thoughts and Strategic Imperatives

To preserve American leadership and secure the orbital commons against revisionist aggression, the United States must decisively reject the siren song of unilateral restraint and unverifiable arms control. Treaties proposed by Beijing and Moscow regarding "no first placement" of weapons in space are transparently asymmetrical: they seek to shackle democratic transparency while leaving totalitarian civil-military apparatuses free to develop and conceal dual-use counterspace capabilities.

Deterrence in the space domain cannot rest on paper agreements or abstract norms of behavior; it must rest upon technological superiority, visible resilience, and undeniable denial-and-punishment calculus. The path forward requires a resolute commitment to several core pillars:

Unrelenting Innovation: The Department of Defense and the U.S. Space Force must accelerate the operational cadence of next-generation reusable space systems, pushing the boundaries of payload capacity, quantum inertial navigation, and rapid-response turnaround times.

Architectural Resilience: Transitioning away from vulnerable, exquisite mega-satellites toward proliferated, disaggregated Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations and on-orbit servicing vehicles will ensure that the destruction of any single asset does not disable vital national security networks.

Proactive Space Domain Awareness (SDA): Advanced multi-phenomenology tracking must provide real-time characterization of proximity operations, ensuring that hostile orbital maneuvers are met with immediate attribution and credible counterspace responses.

Commercial and Alliance Synergy: Harnessing the dynamic velocity of American commercial space innovation—coupled with deep aerospace intelligence-sharing across AUKUS and Five Eyes alliances—creates an impenetrable wall of technological and strategic advantages that no adversary can match through centralized state planning alone.

Ultimately, space is no longer a pristine sanctuary for scientific cooperation; it is a primary theater of geopolitical competition. By anchoring defense policy in timeless principles of realism, technological primacy, and unwavering strength, the United States can ensure that the heavens remain open, free, and secure for generations of free peoples to come.

text:
Han Yu Opposes the Worship of the Buddha’s Bone

A Memorial to the Emperor on the Buddha’s Relic

By Han Yu (768–824 AD), Tang Dynasty

Your Majesty,

I humbly submit the following:

Buddhism is nothing more than a religious teaching that originated among foreign peoples once regarded as barbarians by the Chinese. It was introduced into China during the Later Han Dynasty. In ancient times, China had never known such a religion.

In ancient times, the Yellow Emperor ruled for one hundred years and lived to the age of 110. Shaohao ruled for eighty years and lived to be 100. Zhuanxu ruled for seventy-nine years and lived to be ninety-eight. Emperor Ku ruled for seventy years and lived to be 105. Emperor Yao ruled for ninety-eight years and lived to be 118. Both Emperor Shun and Emperor Yu lived to be 100.

During those times, the country enjoyed peace and prosperity, and ordinary people lived happy, healthy, and long lives. Yet Buddhism did not even exist in China.

Later, King Tang, the founder of the Shang Dynasty, also lived to be 100. His descendant Taiwu ruled for seventy-five years, and King Wuding ruled for fifty-nine years. Although historical records do not tell us exactly how long they lived, judging from the lengths of their reigns, they probably lived to be at least a hundred years old.

King Wen of Zhou lived to be ninety-seven, King Wu lived to be ninety-three, and King Mu ruled for a hundred years.

Buddhism had still not entered China during any of these periods. Clearly, the peace, prosperity, and longevity enjoyed by the people had nothing whatsoever to do with worshipping the Buddha.

Buddhism first appeared in China during the reign of Emperor Ming of the Han Dynasty. Yet Emperor Ming himself ruled for only eighteen years.

After his time, disorder, rebellion, and the collapse of dynasties followed one another, and rulers seldom enjoyed long reigns.

During the Liu Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Northern Wei, and subsequent dynasties, rulers became increasingly devoted to Buddhism. Yet their dynasties grew even shorter-lived.

The only apparent exception was Emperor Wu of the Liang Dynasty, who ruled for forty-eight years.

He was extraordinarily devoted to Buddhism. On three separate occasions, he offered himself to Buddhist monasteries. He abolished the use of sacrificial animals in ancestral ceremonies, ate only one meal a day, and restricted his diet to vegetables and fruit.

And what happened to him in the end?

He was trapped by the rebel general Hou Jing and starved to death in his palace at Taicheng. Shortly afterward, his dynasty collapsed as well.

He worshipped the Buddha in the hope of receiving blessings, but instead brought disaster upon himself.

From these examples, surely it is obvious that Buddhism is not worthy of our worship.

When Emperor Gaozu, the founder of our great Tang Dynasty, first came to power after receiving the throne from the Sui Dynasty, he considered abolishing Buddhism.

Unfortunately, his ministers lacked the wisdom and foresight necessary to understand the teachings of our ancient sage-kings and the needs of their own times. They failed to explain and develop the emperor's wise intentions or to help him eliminate this harmful practice.

Consequently, the proposal was abandoned.

I have always deeply regretted this.

Your Majesty is a ruler of extraordinary wisdom, virtue, and courage, without equal for hundreds, perhaps thousands, of years.

At the beginning of your reign, you prohibited the ordination of new Buddhist monks, Buddhist nuns, and Taoist priests. You also forbade the construction of new temples and monasteries.

I had always believed that the unfinished ambition of Emperor Gaozu would finally be accomplished under Your Majesty's enlightened rule.

Even if this goal cannot be achieved immediately, surely we must not allow Buddhism to spread and flourish even further!

Yet I have now heard that Your Majesty has ordered Buddhist monks to bring a bone relic of the Buddha from Fengxiang to the capital.

I understand that Your Majesty intends to watch the procession from the imperial tower, have the relic carried into the palace, and then allow various Buddhist temples to receive and worship it in turn.

Although I am a man of limited understanding, I cannot believe that Your Majesty has actually been deceived by Buddhist teachings or sincerely imagines that such ceremonies will bring supernatural blessings and good fortune.

Surely Your Majesty has arranged this spectacle merely because the harvests have been abundant, the people are enjoying prosperous times, and you wish to entertain the residents of the capital with something extraordinary and unusual.

How could a ruler of Your Majesty's intelligence and wisdom genuinely believe in such things?

Unfortunately, ordinary people are easily deceived and difficult to enlighten.

When they see Your Majesty behaving in this manner, they will naturally assume that you sincerely believe in Buddhism.

They will say:

"Even our great and enlightened emperor worships the Buddha with complete devotion! Who are we, mere commoners, to hesitate to sacrifice our own bodies and lives for the Buddha?"

As a result, people will gather in groups of dozens or even hundreds to burn their scalps and fingers as religious offerings.

Others will give away their clothing and money.

From morning until night, they will imitate one another, each afraid of being less devoted than the next.

Old and young alike will rush about participating in these ceremonies, abandoning their work, their livelihoods, and their ordinary responsibilities.

Unless these activities are immediately prohibited, and if the relic continues its journey from temple to temple, some people will undoubtedly go so far as to cut off their own arms or slice flesh from their own bodies as offerings to the Buddha.

Such behavior will corrupt public morals, undermine established customs, and make our country a laughingstock throughout the world.

This is no small matter!

Furthermore, the Buddha himself was a foreigner from a people whose language and customs were entirely different from those of China.

He did not speak our language.

He did not wear our clothing.

He did not teach the principles handed down by our ancient sage-kings.

He did not dress according to our traditional standards.

He knew nothing of the proper obligations between ruler and subject or the traditional bonds of affection between father and son.

Now, suppose the Buddha were still alive today.

Suppose he arrived in our capital as an official representative of his native country, bearing the authority of his own ruler.

Even if Your Majesty graciously agreed to receive him, surely the appropriate treatment would be no more than a single formal audience at the palace, a ceremonial reception, and perhaps the gift of a set of clothing.

Afterward, he would be escorted safely back across the frontier, without being permitted to mislead our people.

If this is how we should treat the Buddha while he was alive, how much less reason is there to treat his remains with such extraordinary reverence?

He has been dead for centuries!

What remains of him is nothing more than a decayed old bone, an unclean remnant of a long-dead foreigner.

How can such a thing possibly be considered suitable for admission into the sacred precincts of the imperial palace?

Confucius himself taught us:

"Respect ghosts and spirits, but keep your distance from them."

In ancient times, when rulers attended funerals or paid their respects to the dead within their territories, they first ordered ritual specialists to perform purification ceremonies using peachwood branches and ceremonial brooms to drive away misfortune.

Only after these precautions had been taken would they proceed with the mourning rituals.

Yet now, for no good reason, Your Majesty proposes to bring a decaying relic into the imperial palace and personally inspect it.

No ritual specialists have been summoned beforehand.

No purification ceremonies have been arranged.

Not one of Your Majesty's ministers has spoken out against this improper act.

Not one of the imperial censors has fulfilled his duty by pointing out this mistake.

I am deeply ashamed of them all!

I therefore respectfully beg Your Majesty to place this bone in the hands of the appropriate officials and order it to be thrown into water or destroyed by fire.

Let this practice be brought to an end once and for all!

Let the doubts of the people be dispelled!

Let future generations be freed from this delusion!

Let everyone throughout the empire understand that the actions of a truly great and enlightened ruler rise immeasurably above the foolishness and superstitions of ordinary people.

Would that not be a magnificent achievement?

Would that not be a cause for the greatest satisfaction?

And if the Buddha truly possesses supernatural powers, if his spirit is capable of bringing disaster upon those who offend him, then let every curse, every calamity, and every punishment fall upon me alone!

Let the Buddha direct all his anger against me!

Heaven itself is my witness.

Whatever misfortune may come upon me, I shall neither complain nor regret a single word I have written.

With the deepest sincerity, devotion, and concern for Your Majesty and our country, I respectfully submit this memorial for your consideration.

Your humble servant, filled with reverence and trembling, submits this petition.

text:
Oct 27, 1962: Air Force Maj. Rudolf Anderson was shot down and killed over Cuba. He was the only American killed by enemy fire in the Cuban Missile Crisis, and his death came on the most dangerous day of the Cold War.

Anderson was a U-2 pilot from South Carolina. He had flown some of the earliest missions photographing the Soviet missile sites. On the morning of Oct 27, during the 12th day of the crisis, he flew another one over eastern Cuba. A Soviet surface-to-air missile exploded near his plane. Fragments pierced his pressure suit, and he was killed.

Kennedy had already decided that if a U-2 was shot down, the US would strike back at the missile site. Many of his advisers now wanted to do exactly that. He held off.

It was a day when everything seemed to go wrong. Another U-2 got lost and strayed into Soviet airspace near Alaska, and Soviet fighters scrambled after it. In the Caribbean, American ships dropped practice depth charges on a Soviet submarine, not knowing it carried a nuclear torpedo. People who were there called it Black Saturday.

That night Robert Kennedy met secretly with the Soviet ambassador and offered a deal. The next morning, Khrushchev announced the missiles would come out of Cuba.

Anderson was the first person to receive the Air Force Cross. His body was returned home weeks later, and he was buried in Greenville, South Carolina.

text:
This is probably the best tweet you will read today. 

A kid who was bad at maths, rejected by 25 universities and turned down by DeepMind three times, went on to build the software that OpenAI, Tesla and Meta now use to train their AI. 

His story is the best argument I've seen for never ever quitting.

He grew up in Hyderabad (India), struggled with maths at school, and ended up at VIT in Vellore. VIT is a kind of college people call tier 2 in India, or probably worse. 

He applied to twelve American universities for a master's with a GRE score of 1420 and was rejected by every one of them. He flew to the United States anyway on a J-1 visa with no real plan, applied to fifteen more programmes, and was turned down by all of them except USC and, through a late admission, NYU in 2010.

At NYU he started working with a researcher named Yann LeCun. Yes the same legendary researcher you’re thinking about. When he looked for jobs, the rejections kept coming. DeepMind said no. Almost everyone said no. His only offer was a test engineering role at Amazon.

Later, he applied to deepmind again, but was rejected again. 

He kept building anyway. Around 2011 he wrote one of the fastest AI inference engines on phones, and still got rejected by DeepMind a third time, and then emailed LeCun one more time. 

That email, along with his open source work, got him into Facebook's AI research lab, where he barely made it through bootcamp. Then senior engineers several levels above him couldn't get a major image model to train, and he, the most junior person in the room, found the bug that had everyone stuck. It was his first real win, almost ten years in.

He went on to co-create PyTorch with a team of three, and then watched management try to shut it down over internal politics. He has said he cried at a bar about it. A few people fought to save it, it launched in 2017, and today it sits underneath a huge share of the AI the world uses. 

His name is Soumith Chintala. 

Today he is Chief Technology Officer at Mira Murati led Thinking Machines Labs. 

When the going gets tough. The tough gets going.

text:
Westyn Ruyter offered A$10,000 for his missing Irish wolfhound, Bundy. A promised reunion in Balingup ended in a no-show, followed by a photograph Ruyter says was an artificial-intelligence fake.

Someone claiming to have found Bundy proposed meeting at a general store in Ruyter’s hometown in Western Australia. Nobody arrived with the dog. Only after the failed meeting did Ruyter ask for further proof.

The sender supplied an image apparently showing Bundy inside a crate. Ruyter said it reused the photograph he had posted on Facebook, with a fake-looking dog bowl and cage bars blurred in front of the dog’s face. The sender then stopped replying.

The image’s artificial-intelligence origin has not been independently authenticated. The offered reward is not an established financial loss: no payment or demand for money is reported in this encounter.

The National Anti-Scam Centre warns that scammers target people searching for missing pets, using generated images as supposed proof they have an animal before demanding money, gift cards or cryptocurrency. That broader warning does not establish that such a demand occurred here.

Edith Cowan University cybersecurity professor Paul Haskell-Dowland says scammers use information shared in community groups to tailor convincing approaches. General scam-prevention guidance is to pause before handing over money or personal information and verify who is receiving it.

Whether Bundy has since been found or the sender resumed contact remains unverified.

#MissingPetScams #ScamAwareness

⚖️ CFTC Sues Utah to Block Gambling Laws Against Kalshi and Prediction Markets

🏛️ Federal Government Takes Legal Action: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced Tuesday that it has sued Utah and Attorney General Derek Brown to prevent the state from enforcing gambling restrictions against federally regulated prediction markets, including Kalshi.

⚖️ Federal Authority at Center of Dispute: The CFTC argues that Congress granted it exclusive jurisdiction over derivatives exchanges, including qualifying event contracts. The agency maintains that Utah cannot use state gambling laws to prohibit transactions conducted on federally registered exchanges.

🎯 Utah Accuses Kalshi of Illegal Gambling: Utah filed its own lawsuit against Kalshi on October 20, alleging that the platform offers illegal gambling involving sports, elections, politics, and other events. State officials argue that federal registration does not exempt prediction markets from Utah's gambling restrictions.

🇺🇸 Legal Battle Expands to 10 States: Utah becomes the tenth state facing legal action from the CFTC over prediction market regulation. The federal agency has also challenged enforcement efforts in Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, and Wisconsin.

👨‍⚖️ Previous Court Ruling Favored Utah: In August, a federal judge ruled that federal commodities law did not prevent Utah from enforcing its gambling restrictions against Kalshi. The company appealed, and the latest CFTC lawsuit introduces a separate federal challenge to the state's authority.

💰 Major Implications for Kalshi and Polymarket: The outcome could determine whether federally regulated prediction platforms can offer sports and political event contracts nationwide without obtaining individual state gambling licenses. A ruling supporting broad federal authority could substantially reduce state regulatory barriers.

🏛️ Supreme Court Showdown Possible: Conflicting federal court decisions have intensified the dispute over whether prediction contracts are financial derivatives or gambling products subject to state regulation. Related petitions are already before the Supreme Court, although the justices have not resolved the nationwide jurisdictional question.

📈 What Happens Next: The CFTC is seeking court orders preventing Utah from investigating or taking enforcement action against covered federally regulated markets. The lawsuit itself does not automatically suspend Utah's existing proceedings, and the broader legal status of prediction markets remains contested.

text:
I want to give my thoughts on the Valve/Steam monopoly discourse from two perspectives:
-someone who has been using Steam for 11 years
-someone who is trying to build a company

tldr; Valve has 75% of the PC game distribution market and Epic Games CEO @TimSweeneyEpic has been going into psychosis on twitter about how this is unfair. Very few people agree with him and there is a pattern of those who do. 

This is going to be a bit of a brain dump because I think there isn't any compelling discourse to be had as it is unbelievably unnuanced. I just want to share some of the thoughts that bridge the gap on this between company building and gaming for people who are in one group but not the other.

Quick background, Steam (made by Valve) is a platform where you can buy games as a consumer or sell them as a developer. As a consumer, Steam handles downloads, updates, social networks, game data syncing and more. Though, rarely used, you can even use Steam to voice call with people. It does everything. I can't really think of something that it doesn't do related to gaming at least for my own purposes. Epic Games Launcher(EGL) handled downloads and some friending features, but their overall ecosystem is much less developed compared to Steam.

Steam takes a 30/25/20 cut of sales from games sold on their platform, based on sale volume. Via Steamworks, Steam also helps developers set up social networks (linked to a players existing friend network), matchmaking for multiplayer games, servers, authentication and more. They take a HUGE load off of developers backs if they need the help. Steam also have recently added a disclaimer that must be used to say if your game is developed using AI-assistance and this is what set off Tim's and co. recent meltdown over Steam (He has been tweaking out about Steam since before 2017 lol)

EGL takes 0% and then 12% based on sale volume. Tim is very outspoken about this and claims that Valve robs developers, and his employees and friends agree with him. There is a debate as to whether or not they are right and it is never ending. We could spend hours talking about the argument:

1. Steam has 75% market share, so not publishing on Steam kills your game
2. Steam being an effective monopoly on the market makes it so that it is virtually impossible to convince those 75% to move anywhere else, causing Steam to not be incentivized to lower the 30% cut they take
Counter argument is that Steam reserves the right to charge whatever they want because the customer base they provide is the source of revenue for the developer.

Notice how above I was mainly talking about the developer experience/power balances on the platforms..

In an almost laughable exercise of corporate soulessness, Tim and co. have forgotten that the gaming industry generates revenue entirely from CONSUMERS.

Img #2 is a tweet from @JNavok, who until today I did not know was a person, QRTing a post from @kiaran_ritchie (an ex-EG employee who's post got community noted on this discourse for being objectively wrong) saying it was a harassment campaign, insinuating that Valve is doing this to protect Steam's image. This is moronic.

If given 5 seconds of thought, he might realize that, on X, a large consumer social media platform, where gamers go to see news and talk about the games they play, that when you espouse complete nonsense about games and the platforms people play them on, the people that you sell to will call you out. Just because you disagree with the VOLUME of people calling you an idiot. 
*Mobs on twitter are not often right, but when the mob is your customers... you should listen because they pay your bills

Unrelated, JNavok who worked in corporate strategy at Square Enix, one of the largest developers in the world also notorious for crushing consumer rights. 
*Japanese consumer rights for gaming are very weird and unfriendly towards consumers. Huge issue and an entirely other topic.

So, we have corporate game devs covering their ears going lalalalala trying to "defend"  devs when the writing is on the wall as to the dissatisfaction with their opinion and takes on the market. As unfortunate as that is to small game developers who could benefit greatly from lower % cuts, there are two major facts about this that is being left out.

First point:
Valve's monopoly over PC games distribution has actually been one of the greatest things to ever happen to the gaming industry. Due to their literal golden goose of the steam store they have reinvested tons of $$ into the industry:
-Bankrolling developers of cross platform gameplay systems like Proton
-Bankrolling Wine developers to improve Linux/Windows compatibility 
-Bankrolling graphics drivers developers
-Funding x86-to-ARM work

Counter-Strike, one of the must successful game series EVER was literally created because Valve hired two modders. This shaped esports massively and the FPS genre... This list doesn't even begin to scratch the SURFACE of what Valve does for the gaming ecosystem.

EG has done serious work as well. Unreal Engine, one of the most used tools for game development ever is funded/created by them, but most of EG's support is for closed-source projects...
*Tim Sweeney is a huge conservationist he's spent hundreds of millions in the US to conserve nature and this is very awesome but not related to his shit takes on the gaming industry lol.

The point I'm trying to make here is that Valve's monopoly allows them to invest in open-source projects that better the gaming ecosystem, and they continue to do this all the time. Also, this gives them a easy dunk in 5% of gamers (linux users) as no other platform has this level of support for linux. Also, this development work that is targeting this 5% ends up being used/and adapted in other works and improving the experience for everybody. ALSO, this goodwill just improves the perception of their platform overall. Epic doesn't even have 0.01% of the community goodwill that Valve does.

I know this is a lot but stay with me it will all tie together:

My steam account has over 200 games in it. One of my favorite games ever, CS:GO, was developed by Valve. I have years of friendships stored in my Steam friend's list. Steam has 75% market share for a variety of reasons and one of them is undoubtedly switching cost. If I switched to Epic's Launcher (EGL), I have to re-friend people, all my games are not in one place, and many other issues.

HOWEVER

Epic Launcher, when I last used it 1 year ago or more.. f*cking sucked. It also sucked 6 years ago. Not even with the bad, UI, slow booting, poor UX way, but an issue I've had for years with EGL is just downloading games! I used to have to wait 24 hours on  100 Mbps internet just to INSTALL AN UPDATE. Epic's game distribution and downloading code was just broken. It would sit at 0Mbps download for hours despite troubleshooting restarts etc. Steam did not have this issue. This was exclusively an issue with me when I was trying to play Fortnite in early high school and a bit over a year ago. This take may be severely out of date, but this was a lasting impact on my experience with the launcher.

Second Point finally!!:
As a consumer... Steam just works! It works, there are very few, if any, issues and everything I could ever need is there. The reason this matters is as consumers we do not owe any company our business. You have the right to chose what service you use, and even if you give me free $60 games every month, if I can't download them why would I care??????

Gaming is a really really really unique industry where feedback is everywhere and very vocal. People are LOUD. A lot of it is noise but there is mountains of data on player retention, game enjoyment and even just general sentiment online about how people are liking games.

Gabe Newell, CEO of Valve: 
“People are happy to pay money if they're getting what they perceive as a great product delivered on their terms.”

This pretty much sums up the problem. From his beautiful forests in North Carolina, Tim (and his friends) have lost touch with the people he is selling to Because his wallet is perceptibly affected by the absolute mogging that Valve does with Steam, he has made the problem about how he + developers feel. Once again, it is an unfortunate reality, but developers are not owed business by consumers, even small ones.

Ok now does this make any sense or how is it relevant to startups?? 

First, as a company you can either be loved or hated for a variety of reasons, or mixed.

When my cofounder and I @kejerial were working on trying to build software for real estate for 3 months, we learned about Yardi, RealPage and others. These companies are hated. The UX sucks, switching costs are high. There are literally job listings for Yardi specialists because the software is so convoluted. These companies exist because without the software real estate management would collapse overnight. There is basically zero choice for large players to switch. Building in spaces like this is hard, as RE companies are quite literally life lined by these software tools. 

Steam has a high switching cost because instead of hooking up your company to a parasitic software, you as a young pre-teen or teenager have sentimental value and convenience tied to a platform that has treated you abundantly well. Sale after sale, improvement after improvement, strong support and more. When I was in a bad financial spot in high school with my family, steam sales were a huge deal! Instead of pirating, I'd wait for the sale cause I knew they were always coming and would let me play with my existing friend group, AND I could download the games...

Stripe, Ramp, and other rockets of my time (as a 21 yr old) are LOVED by the people using them, and they continue to see growth and success. These guys entered the complicated world of accounts management and payment processing, and built an amazing product and now dominate the field. If you can build a better UX for the people paying and doing the work, and won't kill their company by switching them, you can win. 

EG has not done this. The consumer experience on the EGL objectively sucks. 
*They tried to vibe code a better UX, made a tweet saying their launcher opened faster than Valve's, and then got dogged because it was buggy and ugly. Valve has payrolled artists for god knows how much money to make Steam a 3 Michelin Star UX. Epic's strategy was "claude make this less ugly"

It is written in bankruptcies and tears of failed companies. Tim has misunderstood this for 26 years. Tim wrote a public letter in 2000 saying profitability was the core to a succeeding game studio as the explanation to a game studio shutting down. In the consumer space, the $$$ signs coming into a business are tied with the # of people that you can make happy with your product. If that number is too few, it is not necessarily a profitability issue, it is an ICP issue..

I know for a fact Tim and co. understand this core fact, but they have lost the plot in decision making. 

You can offer developers the best terms in the world, because you are a developer and want the best for them, but the money still comes from the gamers!! If the marketplace is falling apart, ugly, and you can't even walk out with your items (download them)...  no one will buy in your marketplace, even if high dollar items are FREE. 

There is a galactic difference between customers who are hostage versus customers who are free to go wherever they want. The pattern of misunderstanding here stems from literal caricatures of the corporate world not understanding what their customers actually want, but look at quarterly earnings and stakeholders meetings as the most important metrics for success

Personally, with my current venture, it has become very easy to laud and sell my product because I know and dream that this will be extremely useful to people. If you have to cry about monopoly or incumbents or anyone upstream of the payer getting shafted, your priorities are wrong. I can not imagine trying to convince someone that, for some reason, they should use my, in every way, inferior product because... the other guy they use is too good??

Anyways. This is random, but in the first 2 weeks when Kevin and I were sitting down with a mentor at Neo, I asked if I sat in a basement and found the cure to cancer but never shared it, if that was valuable. Her answer was "No". If no one can use it or benefit from it, it is not valuable. This is extremely simple and generally drives our economy. If your value delivery machine is ugly and slow and broken... no value is created and no one will use your products!!

This brain dump is filled with generalizations. For example, a company can make people happy by giving away free money, but this will not mean they are a good company. I am not trying to write a lean-verifiable argument of how this works. End of the day, all I want to do is share with some people how ridiculous it is that a billionaire game studio developer is arguing with consumers about how they should or should not enjoy the thing that they pay for.

Also, I can't confirm, but I don't think a single Valve employee has commented on this at all lol. 

ALSO, I didn't cover it much but basically Valve added a AI disclosure, and Tim thinks this is unfair to small devs and is similar to disclosing the political party of the developer... He is trying to construct a moral argument in favor of devs so that the negative attention of AI in some circles is not forced on to them..

Valve, saw people in the Steam user base wanted to know if something used AI to make it, so they added it as it also aligns with their values. Customers win again!

Washington State 

NATIONAL GUARD 

'NEIGHBORHOOD WATCH'

Clark County ▪︎ Usland County ▪︎ King County ▪︎ Pierce County ▪︎ Snohomish County ▪︎ Thurston County

National Guard and DOJ expected around Washington's 2026 midterm election

Oct. 27, 2026

People register to vote at the King County Elections headquarters on Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 5, 2024, in Renton, Wash. (photo)

Six Washington counties have accepted Gov. Bob Ferguson's offer to have unarmed, plainclothes National Guard members help with security around the 2026 midterms — an election that has drawn higher-than-usual attention from federal authorities.

"This is not intended to be a visible presence, and folks are not going to see Guard members, for example, stationed at drop boxes," said King County Elections Chief of Staff Kendall Hodson, adding that guardsmen will report to the elections director and supplement existing security with "additional eyes and ears."

The governor recently sent a letter to the state’s county election officials, offering to send National Guard members to help with security. The following counties accepted:

Clark County
Island County
King County
Pierce County
Snohomish County
Thurston County

Spokane County declined the offer.

The Guard's "Neighborhood Watch" mission will begin in some counties later this week, ahead of Nov. 3. 

Guard members in civilian clothes will observe voting sites without interacting with voters. They will alert local authorities if problems arise. Members will be trained on the mission's limits, including laws on how close a person may be to a drop box.

In 2024, then-Gov. Jay Inslee placed National Guard members on strict standby to support local police departments if requested. 

This time, the Guard members are being integrated into local county election operations. They remain under the governor’s command, but will carry out security plans developed with county election officials.

In Snohomish County, that includes watching the county's 38 drop boxes during evening and overnight hours.

"Guard members will not empty boxes, handle ballots, interact with voters, or act in any enforcement capacity," the Snohomish County Auditor's Office told KUOW.

Clark County Auditor Greg Kimsey said Guard members will also watch drop boxes there. That includes the one at Fisher's Landing in Vancouver, the same location where someone set a drop box on fire two years ago, destroying hundreds of ballots.

“It was horrible. It was horrible. It was a direct attack on democracy,” Kimsey said. “You don't get much more direct than that.”

Clark County has since strengthened fire suppression and added alert sensors at drop boxes. The county is also installing cameras at its 22 official ballot drop boxes.

Ferguson's letter to the counties cited the Vancouver ballot box attack. He also referenced the envelopes containing white-powder that were recently mailed to Washington state officials as reasons for added security in this election.

Despite accepting the presence of the National Guard, Kimsey in Clark County observed that local political tensions are not what they were in 2024.

"The temperature has lowered quite a bit from two years ago, in fact, quite dramatically so," Kimsey said, noting that while security remains top of mind, the atmosphere surrounding the county's highly-contested 3rd Congressional District race feels "a lot calmer."

Federal officials focus on Washington

In King County, state National Guard members won’t be the only ones observing the voting process. 

The Department of Justice told County Elections Director Julie Wise it will send monitors on Election Day. The Secretary of State's office confirmed that federal monitors will also go to Yakima County.

Brionna Aho, spokesperson with the governor’s office, also noted that, "There is no coordination between the Washington National Guard and federal election monitors.”

"They don't eat. They don't sleep. They don't complain. They don't ask for raises. They don't need veterans' benefits. And not one of them has ever leaked classified information to The New York Times."

⚖️ Florida Murder Suspect, 74, Offers to Plead Guilty for Philly Cheesesteak, Fries and Pepsi, but Judge Refuses

🥪 Unusual Courtroom Proposal: Robert Kessler, 74, stunned a Florida courtroom when he offered to plead guilty to first degree murder in exchange for a Philly cheesesteak with onions and mayonnaise, an order of fries, and a 20 ounce Pepsi.

⚖️ Judge Rejects the Deal: Hillsborough County Circuit Judge Nick Nazaretian refused the unusual proposal, saying that providing food in exchange for a guilty plea would be inappropriate. The judge remarked that he had never encountered such a request in nearly 40 years of legal experience.

🚨 Disturbing Murder Allegations: Kessler is accused of murdering and dismembering 47 year old Stephanie Crone Overholts in 2021. Her remains were discovered in McKay Bay near Tampa. Investigators reportedly recovered evidence linking Kessler to the killing, including the victim's blood inside his residence and vehicle.

💰 Suspect Claims Deal Would Save Taxpayers: During jury selection on October 26, Kessler suggested that accepting his proposal would spare taxpayers the expense of a murder trial. He was considering an open guilty plea that would result in life imprisonment.

👨‍⚖️ Trial Moves Forward: After the judge rejected his request, Kessler declined to plead guilty and instructed the court to continue jury selection. He faces charges of first degree murder and abuse of a dead body, with a mandatory life sentence if convicted of murder.

🔍 Legal Implications: Although defendants can plead guilty without negotiating a reduced sentence, judges must ensure guilty pleas are voluntary and legally valid. Offering a meal as an incentive could raise serious concerns about the integrity of the proceedings.

THE EVIDENCE™ — HOLLYWOOD & POLITICAL SATIRE

ILHAN OMAR AND MATT DAMON TO STAR IN NEXT JASON BOURNE MOVIE

The Bourne Identity Crisis — Jason Bourne Has Survived the CIA, International Assassins, and Government Conspiracies. Now He Faces His Most Dangerous Assignment: Surviving Washington With Ilhan Omar.

By Kim Wojcinski | USA Best Selling Author
SATIRE — FICTIONAL NEWS REPORT

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

HOLLYWOOD — In a casting decision that has reportedly left Hollywood executives, intelligence officials, and congressional ethics attorneys reaching for emergency medication, Universal Pictures has announced a fictional new installment of the Jason Bourne franchise starring Matt Damon alongside Minnesota Congresswoman Ilhan Omar. Tentatively titled The Bourne Identity Crisis, the production promises to take America's most resourceful intelligence operative into territory considerably more dangerous than Moscow, Berlin, or Baghdad: the United States Congress.

Studio executives reportedly selected Omar after concluding that Bourne needed a partner with extensive experience navigating political controversy, hostile questioning, competing narratives, and televised confrontations. Although Bourne has spent his career escaping government agents determined to eliminate him, his new partner operates in an environment where adversaries attempt to destroy one another politically while addressing each other as "my distinguished colleague."

Damon allegedly welcomed the casting decision after reviewing Omar's congressional career. "Jason has survived professional assassins, international conspiracies, and intelligence agencies with virtually unlimited resources. But he's never encountered someone who can turn a five-minute question into a forty-five-minute argument about institutional prejudice, foreign policy, and why the question itself should never have been asked."

According to the fictional screenplay, Omar agreed to participate after producers assured her that she would not be required to answer questions about the plot until the final scene, at which point she could accuse the screenwriters of conducting a politically motivated investigation.

THE MISSION: FIND THE TRUTH WITHOUT OFFENDING ANYONE

The film opens in Washington, D.C., where Bourne awakens inside a congressional hearing room with no memory of how he arrived or why seventeen members of Congress are demanding answers about an intelligence operation he has never heard of. A classified folder sits before him, stamped TOP SECRET, although portions have already appeared on social media and a cable news network is reporting that unnamed officials have confirmed its contents.

Omar enters carrying a congressional briefing binder, three press releases, and a list of questions she considers inappropriate.

"Bourne, you need to understand something about Washington," she explains. "The purpose of a congressional investigation isn't necessarily to discover what happened. It's to determine which version of what happened benefits your political position."

Bourne studies the documents and asks whether the committee intends to interview the people directly involved.

"Only after we've decided what they're supposed to say."

His first assignment is to investigate a mysterious intelligence program that has consumed billions of taxpayer dollars without producing measurable results. Bourne naturally assumes that an operation of such magnitude must involve covert personnel, sophisticated surveillance, or an international threat.

Omar explains that he has misunderstood the nature of the program.

"It's called a federal initiative, Jason. Once Congress funds it, the important thing is to keep funding it. Whether it accomplishes anything is a separate question."

Bourne asks what happens when taxpayers demand an accounting.

"That's when we establish an oversight committee."

JASON BOURNE MEETS THE CONGRESSIONAL DOUBLE STANDARD

The investigation takes Bourne and Omar to Minneapolis, where they encounter a fictional network of political consultants, federal grant administrators, community organizations, and government contractors who have transformed public funding into an elaborate exercise in paperwork, political influence, and institutional self-preservation.

Bourne discovers that ordinary citizens applying for government assistance must document their identities, income, residency, eligibility, and financial circumstances. Organizations seeking multimillion-dollar grants, however, can sometimes operate within administrative systems so complicated that determining where the money ultimately went requires another taxpayer-funded investigation.

"Something is wrong with this system," Bourne observes.

Omar agrees, although not for the reason he expects.

"Absolutely. We need additional funding to determine why the previous funding failed to produce the results promised by the people who requested the funding."

Bourne suggests following the money, examining the contracts, identifying the responsible officials, and referring evidence of criminal conduct to prosecutors.

Omar looks horrified.

"Jason, you can't simply investigate people because financial records suggest something improper. You have to consider how the investigation might be interpreted politically."

Bourne reminds her that financial misconduct is not an ethnicity, religion, political affiliation, or protected classification.

"That's an interesting theory," she responds. "Have you considered how it would sound on television?"

The exchange establishes the film's central conflict. Bourne believes evidence should determine conclusions, while Washington's political machinery is considerably more interested in determining which conclusions can survive the next election.

THE MOST DANGEROUS ORGANIZATION IN WASHINGTON

Bourne eventually discovers that the intelligence operation he is investigating is controlled by a secretive organization known as THE COMMITTEE, a bipartisan collection of senior officials whose greatest talent is ensuring that nobody can identify the person responsible for any particular decision.

Unlike the CIA's legendary Treadstone program, THE COMMITTEE does not train assassins or deploy covert operatives. Its members prefer a subtler approach: administrative obstruction, procedural immunity, strategic leaks, and investigations that continue until the original controversy has been forgotten.

Its most effective weapon is a process known as RESPONSIBILITY TRANSFERENCE, under which every official involved in a decision can demonstrate that final authority belonged to someone else.

When Bourne infiltrates its headquarters, he discovers an extraordinary organizational structure. Every department has an oversight division, every oversight division has an independent review board, and every review board reports to a congressional committee whose members insist they were never informed of the underlying problem.

The entire operation occupies seventeen floors of a federal building and employs 4,800 people.

Bourne asks to meet the person in charge.

The receptionist informs him that the position has been vacant for six years, although the office continues receiving an annual operating appropriation of $860 million.

Bourne recognizes the danger immediately. He has encountered an organization that cannot be defeated because nobody will admit to running it.

THE CHASE SCENE HOLLYWOOD HAS BEEN WAITING FOR

The film's signature action sequence begins when Bourne obtains a classified financial report showing that federal expenditures have been routed through numerous agencies without a coherent accounting of their original purpose.

Within minutes, federal agents converge on his location, triggering a spectacular motorcycle chase through downtown Washington. Armored SUVs pursue him past the Treasury Department, FBI headquarters, and Capitol complex while Omar, riding behind him, conducts an unscheduled interview with a cable news correspondent.

"Jason, slow down!" she shouts.

"Are they gaining on us?"

"No! The camera crew can't keep up!"

Bourne accelerates through an intersection, narrowly avoids a government motorcade, and executes a maneuver that sends two pursuing vehicles crashing into a congressional parking barrier.

Omar immediately demands an investigation into the barrier's discriminatory impact on elected officials attempting to escape federal accountability.

The pursuit ends outside the Capitol, where agents surround Bourne and demand identification. He produces a passport, military credentials, and a classified CIA personnel file, but the commanding officer refuses to release him without additional verification.

Omar approaches the officer and announces that Bourne is now serving as her congressional consultant.

The situation changes immediately.

The agents return his identification, apologize for the inconvenience, and ask whether his travel expenses should be reimbursed through the congressional office budget.

Bourne stares at Omar.

"That's all it takes?"

"Jason, you spent twenty years learning how to defeat government security. I learned how to make government security work for me."

THE CONGRESSIONAL HEARING FROM HELL

The film's most politically explosive scene occurs when Bourne appears before a fictional congressional oversight committee to present the financial evidence he has recovered.

He arrives expecting a serious examination of missing funds, contradictory testimony, and questionable expenditures. Instead, he discovers that committee members have already prepared their opening statements, issued press releases, and scheduled appearances on competing television networks.

One congressman demands to know whether Bourne's investigation was motivated by political prejudice. Another insists that the entire controversy is an attempt to distract voters from the opposing party's failures. A third delivers a passionate speech about government transparency before requesting that all supporting documents be placed under seal.

When Bourne finally attempts to explain the evidence, Omar interrupts with a procedural objection.

"Before we proceed, I want to know whether Mr. Bourne has considered the consequences of allowing these allegations to circulate without appropriate political context."

Bourne replies that the records establish what happened, regardless of how the findings might affect anyone's preferred narrative.

A committee member immediately asks whether his refusal to consider political context demonstrates an unconscious institutional bias.

Bourne pauses. For a man trained to survive interrogation, torture, and psychological manipulation, he finds the exchange unusually challenging.

"Congresswoman, are you suggesting that evidence becomes invalid when the conclusions are politically inconvenient?"

Omar leans toward her microphone.

"I'm suggesting that your question reflects a troubling misunderstanding of how Washington works."

Bourne looks toward the committee chairman.

"Is anyone here actually interested in finding out what happened to the money?"

The chairman checks his watch.

"Mr. Bourne, your time has expired."

THE $14.7 BILLION DISCOVERY

In the final act, Bourne bypasses congressional oversight entirely and infiltrates a secure federal records facility, where he discovers the financial history of the mysterious intelligence operation.

The documents reveal that Washington has spent $14.7 billion over eleven years funding a program originally established to assess whether a separate government agency should be created to evaluate the effectiveness of existing government agencies.

The proposed agency was never established. Nevertheless, the preliminary planning office continued operating, its budget expanded annually, and several congressional committees began conducting oversight hearings into the reasons the project had not progressed.

The resulting investigations generated additional appropriations, outside consulting contracts, administrative positions, and a comprehensive modernization initiative that produced a 9,000-page report recommending further study.

Bourne examines the records in disbelief.

"Fourteen point seven billion dollars, and they never created the agency?"

Omar studies the figures.

"That's not entirely fair, Jason. They created thousands of jobs."

"Doing what?"

"Preparing to determine what the agency would do if Congress ever authorized it."

Bourne demands to know who approved the expenditures.

Omar gestures toward the congressional authorization records.

"Both parties voted for the appropriations. Naturally, both parties are now demanding an investigation into how the money was spent."

For the first time, Bourne realizes that the conspiracy he has uncovered requires neither secrecy nor sophisticated deception. The expenditures have been documented, authorized, and defended through the ordinary machinery of government. Every participant has a plausible explanation, every failure has an administrative justification, and every proposed reform requires another appropriation.

He has finally encountered an adversary capable of absorbing unlimited punishment without changing its behavior.

HOLLYWOOD'S MOST UNLIKELY PARTNERSHIP

According to fictional studio insiders, the production has already generated enthusiasm among political consultants who believe the Bourne franchise offers an opportunity to portray Washington's dysfunction without requiring viewers to understand congressional procedure.

Omar's character reportedly provides a unique counterpoint to Bourne's uncompromising pursuit of facts. Whenever he discovers evidence that threatens an established political narrative, she offers an alternative interpretation suitable for immediate broadcast. Whenever he demands individual accountability, she recommends a broader discussion of historical circumstances. And whenever someone asks a question she would prefer not to answer, she reminds the audience that the timing of the question is itself suspicious.

The pairing reportedly inspired producers to consider expanding the franchise into a series of political thrillers featuring elected officials from both parties. Proposed future installments include The Bourne Filibuster, The Bourne Continuing Resolution, and The Bourne Executive Privilege, in which the principal characters attempt to locate a government document that everyone claims exists but nobody is willing to produce.

One fictional executive suggested that Congress itself should serve as the franchise's permanent antagonist.

"It's perfect," he explained. "The audience already knows the villain, the organization has an unlimited budget, and every time somebody gets caught doing something questionable, the next investigation becomes another sequel."

THE VERDICT

The original Jason Bourne films presented an intelligence operative struggling to recover his identity while exposing government institutions determined to conceal their activities. The Bourne Identity Crisis extends that premise into a political environment where the central obstacle is not discovering the truth but persuading elected officials that it deserves consideration when the findings threaten their interests.

Casting Ilhan Omar opposite Matt Damon gives the fictional production its central satirical contrast. Bourne represents the relentless investigator who follows evidence wherever it leads; Omar represents the political operator whose survival depends upon controlling the argument, challenging the premise, and ensuring that uncomfortable questions never receive more attention than the people asking them.

The broader target, however, is Washington's institutional culture. Republicans and Democrats alike have demonstrated a remarkable capacity to demand accountability from their opponents while discovering procedural complications, mitigating circumstances, and constitutional objections whenever the investigation turns toward their own political allies.

Bourne's problem is that he assumes every operation has an objective, every decision has an accountable authority, and every investigation should eventually produce a conclusion. Those assumptions have served him well against the world's most formidable intelligence organizations. In Washington, they qualify him as dangerously inexperienced.

The fictional studio has reportedly approved the film's official promotional slogan:

JASON BOURNE CAN ESCAPE THE CIA.

HE CAN OUTRUN PROFESSIONAL ASSASSINS.

HE CAN EXPOSE INTERNATIONAL CONSPIRACIES.

BUT CAN HE SURVIVE ILHAN OMAR AND THE UNITED STATES CONGRESS?

The final scene shows Bourne abandoning Washington after discovering that the government has established a special committee to investigate his unauthorized disclosure of records documenting the government's failure to account for $14.7 billion.

As he disappears into the crowd, Omar receives an urgent call from the committee chairman.

Congress has approved another $2.3 billion to determine whether the original $14.7 billion was spent appropriately.

The chairman wants Bourne appointed as the investigation's special consultant.

Omar smiles.

"Unfortunately, he's unavailable."

"Where is he?"

"Somewhere in Eastern Europe, fighting international terrorists."

The chairman sounds disappointed.

"Isn't that dangerous?"

Omar looks toward the Capitol.

"Not compared to working here."

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

Washington State advocates renew calls for state to limit feds’ access to license data

State officials have erected several barriers to block immigration authorities from getting data to detain immigrants. Critics say there are still holes.

Oct. 27, 2026

A new court ruling allows ICE to use Medicaid data, alarming some states and advocates who warn it could have a chilling effect on immigrant families accessing health care.

SEATTLE — Chris Megargee volunteers at a Shoreline Home Depot to help day laborers frequently targeted by federal immigration authorities. 

As part of the adopt-a-corner program, Megargee and other volunteers provide breakfast and share information so the workers, who are often non-citizens, know their rights if U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents come. 

Since January, ICE officials have detained half a dozen men there, including one this month, who drove their cars to the Home Depot, Megargee said. 

Before arresting each, ICE agents entered the license plate numbers on those cars into a database, and received car registration information to identify the driver, Megargee alleged.

Advocates gathered in Seattle on Tuesday to continue their push for Washington state officials to do more to restrict the ability of the feds to get information from the license plate database.

“We need you to act and slow down this mass deportation and detention machine by continuing to cut off access to the Department of Licensing data that is being used for immigration enforcement,” said ** Lucía Vázquez Martínez, field director for Service Employees International Union 775. 

Gov. Bob Ferguson noted his administration has acted to curb unfettered access to the state’s data.

“My team has worked to limit Customs and Border Protection access for immigration enforcement, while maintaining access necessary to protect public safety, such as human trafficking investigations that require real-time access to data to protect vulnerable Washingtonians,” he said in a statement Tuesday. 

“Looking ahead to the next two years, this will be an ongoing process for us to adapt to what (the) federal government does next to work around what we do to protect our data,” Ferguson added.

These concerns date back years, but have intensified as President Donald Trump’s mass deportation campaign has grown in Washington, with surges seen in recent months.

University of Washington researchers connected 356 arrests to federal queries for license data between August 2025 and Oct. 13 of this year. In the first five months of this year, agencies housed under the U.S. Department of Homeland Security searched state Department of Licensing driver and vehicle data over 1 million times, according to the university’s Center for Human Rights.

Washington is one of 19 states that offer driver’s licenses regardless of immigration status. Others require warrants or court orders for federal agencies to access state-held license and vehicle data for immigration purposes, according to the UW researchers. Washington does not.

Ferguson spokesperson Brionna Aho said Tuesday that “our team is reviewing what other states have done, and what is lawful, to require judicial warrants for civil immigration-related requests.”

What the state has already done
Last November, Washington officials cut off ICE’s ability to get this data. This was later expanded to Homeland Security Investigations, also known as HSI.

Between November 2025 and Oct. 12, the Washington State Patrol blocked over 174,000 search attempts from federal agencies, including 89,000 from Customs and Border Protection, 45,000 from HSI and nearly 40,000 from ICE, according to the governor’s office. However, researchers say millions more searches from the Department of Homeland Security have still gone through.

Jon Levine, The Washington Free Beacon
Abdul E-Sayed wrote that it was “troubling” that the United States killed the al Qaeda chief, Ayman al-Zawahiri—who is widely considered the mastermind of 9/11—in a 2022 targeted drone strike.

Killing al-Zawahiri was “a fig leaf” to cover up the disastrous U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan, El-Sayed wrote in 2022, the Washington Free Beacon can reveal.

In the piece, “Projecting Strength Abroad Isn’t Simply About Killing Terrorists. It’s About Standing Up to Despots, Too,” which was published in the New Republic on Aug. 5, 2022.
El-Sayed spoke out against the CIA drone strike that successfully took out al-Zawahiri, a fellow Egyptian who’d joined the Muslim Brotherhood as a teenager and ultimately rose to lead al Qaeda.

“President Biden is using the strike to bolster his approval here at home. It is troubling to watch yet another American president flog ‘War on Terror’ themes to resurrect a laggard term,” El-Sayed sniffed in the article.

El-Sayed went on to accuse Biden of launching the attack on al-Zawahiri—who’d been on the FBI’s 10 most wanted terrorist list for almost 21 years—as a way to arrest sliding approval numbers stemming from the disastrous United States withdrawal from Afghanistan.

“This strike,” he went on, “offers the Biden administration a fig leaf, demonstrating that even in Taliban hands, Afghanistan is not off-limits for direct action against terrorist targets,” El-Sayed wrote, adding that Biden did it in order to “project strength” for Democrats heading into the midterm elections that year.
